Initial specification:

- [e004] Update from Quinn: the owning team of label-print is set to `team-routing`, effective now.
- [e005] Update from Nils: the owning team of depot-svc is set to `team-routing`, effective now.
- [e006] Zed confirmed in writing that the owning team of carrier-hub changes to `team-parcels`.
- [e007] After the review, the team settled on `team-customs` for the owning team of route-planner.
- [e008] After the review, the team settled on `team-carriers` for the owning team of slot-booking.
- [e009] Approved: `geo-fence` joins the dependencies of parcel-track.
- [e010] From now on, the dependencies of geo-fence include `manifest-gen`.
- [e011] Approved: `label-print` joins the dependencies of manifest-gen.
- [e012] From now on, the dependencies of depot-svc include `label-print`.
- [e013] Approved: `parcel-track` joins the dependencies of carrier-hub.
- [e014] From now on, the dependencies of route-planner include `slot-booking`.
- [e015] Decision: the on-call engineer for parcel-track is now `sami`.
- [e016] Update from Lars: the on-call engineer for geo-fence is set to `rosa`, effective now.

Rules for this task:
- A value changes only by an event that decides, corrects, adds, removes, renames, runs or restores it. A proposal, a question, a link or a quote of an old page changes nothing.
- A correction or a new decision replaces the earlier value. The earlier value is then superseded.
- The initial specification gives the first value of each item.
- A service has one owning team at a time. A new owner replaces the earlier owner.
- A rename gives a team a new name. The team keeps its services. Every reference to the old name means the new name.
- The dependencies of a service are the services in its own dependency list. These are its direct dependencies. A dependency of a dependency is not counted.
- A service has one on-call engineer at a time. A new assignment replaces the earlier one.
Every event has a label of the form [eNNN] with a three-digit number. A higher number is later in time. A later event can change or cancel an earlier one.
Some material quotes old pages or copies for history. A quote of that kind is not a new statement.
